Build dynamic-filter control points from a tracked period curve

Source: R/dynamic_filter_controls.R
dynamic_filter_controls.Rd

The dynamic_filter_controls function converts a tracked period curve [depth, period] into pass band control points for dynamic_filter. This replaces the interactive clicking of lower/upper frequency boundaries on an evolutionary spectrum in Acycle (dynamic_filter_lang.m) by a reproducible, non-interactive step. The curve can come directly from the WaverideR functions track_period_wavelet (first two columns: depth, period) or completed_series (depth, period), so cycles already tracked in a wavelet scalogram can be filtered with the Acycle dynamic filter. The centre frequency is 1 / period; the pass band is f_centre * (1 -/+ rel_bandwidth / 2), i.e. rel_bandwidth is the half-power bandwidth relative to the centre frequency (the band is symmetric in frequency, as the Acycle Gaussian response is). Written for the R translation of Acycle v3.1 dynamic filtering (Mingsong Li); no MATLAB equivalent.

Usage

dynamic_filter_controls(
  tracked = NULL,
  rel_bandwidth = 0.2,
  n_points = NULL,
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

tracked

Tracked period curve of the cycle (matrix or data frame whose first two columns are depth/time and period in the same depth/time unit, period > 0; further columns are ignored), e.g. the output of track_period_wavelet or completed_series. Rows with non-finite values are dropped, rows are sorted by depth and duplicated depths are removed (first kept). Required (Default=NULL).

rel_bandwidth

Half-power bandwidth of the pass band relative to the centre frequency 1 / period (numeric, > 0 and < 2): the band is f_centre * (1 -/+ rel_bandwidth / 2), so larger values give a wider band. Default=0.2.

n_points

Maximum number of control points (integer, >= 1, or NULL). When the tracked curve has more rows, it is linearly interpolated to n_points evenly spaced depths spanning the (clipped) curve (n_points=1 gives one point at the middle). NULL keeps all rows. Default=NULL.

data

Series that will be filtered (two-column matrix or data frame, depth/time in column 1, or NULL). When given, control points outside its depth range are removed, because dynamic_filter requires control depths inside the data range. Default=NULL.

Value

A matrix with columns depth, f_low, f_high and f_centre, directly usable as the controls argument of dynamic_filter.

References

Arts, M., 2023. WaverideR: Extracting signals from wavelet spectra. <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=WaverideR>

Li, M., Hinnov, L., Kump, L., 2019. Acycle: Time-series analysis software for paleoclimate research and education. Computers & Geosciences 127, 12-22. <doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2019.02.011>

Author

Michiel Arts

Examples

# \donttest{
depth <- seq(0, 300, by = 1)
period <- 5 + 10 * depth / 300
ctrl <- dynamic_filter_controls(tracked = cbind(depth, period),
  rel_bandwidth = 0.3, n_points = 20)
head(ctrl)
#>         depth     f_low    f_high  f_centre
#> [1,]  0.00000 0.1700000 0.2300000 0.2000000
#> [2,] 15.78947 0.1538095 0.2080952 0.1809524
#> [3,] 31.57895 0.1404348 0.1900000 0.1652174
#> [4,] 47.36842 0.1292000 0.1748000 0.1520000
#> [5,] 63.15789 0.1196296 0.1618519 0.1407407
#> [6,] 78.94737 0.1113793 0.1506897 0.1310345
# }
